stableMappingPatterns.name: optionType copied from trade.bondoption.optiontype to payout.optionpayout.optiontype
stableMappingPatterns.explanation: Option type values in the FPML bond/convertible bond option trades are preserved and placed into the CDM OptionPayout.optionType field.
stableMappingPatterns.whyItWorksThisWay: Option type represents an option semantic that is preserved across the source and CDM target and therefore is mapped directly without transformation.

repeatedNonLiteralTransformations.name: date/time trimmed to date-only
repeatedNonLiteralTransformations.description: Date/time values in FPML are trimmed/normalized to date-only (YYYY-MM-DD) in the CDM.
repeatedNonLiteralTransformations.sourceSide: FPML dateTime (often with timezone or time component)
notes: Representative notes mention 'trim timezone to YYYY-MM-DD' and 'strip timezone/time to date-only' across examples.
Applied to trade dates and centers where present.

repeatedNonLiteralTransformations.name: party role mapping: buyer/seller -> payer/receiver
repeatedNonLiteralTransformations.description: FPML buyer and seller references are mapped to CDM counterparties and used as OptionPayout buyer/payer and seller/receiver roles (buyer->payer, seller->receiver).
repeatedNonLiteralTransformations.sourceSide: FPML buyer/seller references and trade party references
repeatedNonLiteralTransformations.targetSide: CDM counterparty entries and OptionPayout buyer/payer and seller/receiver
notes: Examples show buyer reference mapping to counterparty and OptionPayout buyer/payer; seller to counterparty and OptionPayout seller/receiver.
There is repeated uncertainty about payer/receiver inversion which suggests mapping exists but its direction/semantics should be verified.

repeatedNonLiteralTransformations.name: numberOfOptions -> tradeLot.quantity and parValue -> multiplier
repeatedNonLiteralTransformations.description: FPML numberOfOptions becomes a CDM quantity; FPML parValue becomes a multiplier on the CDM trade lot.
notes: Represented in cb-option mapping: 'numberOfOptions->quantity, parValue->multiplier, currency->currency'.

repeatedNonLiteralTransformations.name: premium mapped to transferHistory entry
repeatedNonLiteralTransformations.description: FPML premium information is represented as a transfer/transferHistory entry in the CDM.
notes: bond-option shows premium mapped to transferHistory; appears as a transfer wrapper in target.

repeatedNonLiteralTransformations.name: notional/par value mapping to tradeLot quantity
repeatedNonLiteralTransformations.description: FPML notional/par value is used to produce tradeLot.quantity in CDM (notional-sized quantity representation).
repeatedNonLiteralTransformations.sourceSide: FPML notional / nominal / par value fields
repeatedNonLiteralTransformations.targetSide: CDM tradeLot.quantity (and possibly multiplier per above)
notes: bond-option highlights notional mapped to tradeLot quantity.

repeatedNonLiteralTransformations.name: currency preserved
repeatedNonLiteralTransformations.description: Currency values are preserved from FPML into CDM currency fields for quantity/amounts.

tentativeRepeatedPatterns.description: Option-specific terms repeatedly map from trade.bondoption.optiontype into payout.optionpayout.optiontype.

variantsAndExceptions.name: OptionPayout.payerReceiver inversion
variantsAndExceptions.description: Several examples show payer/receiver values that appear inverted relative to FPML buyer/seller; mapping direction may differ or be intentionally inverted in CDM.
variantsAndExceptions.impactOnGeneralization: Mapping of buyer/seller to payer/receiver should be treated as a variant; automated rules should include a verification step. This reduces confidence in blindly swapping roles without checking contextual semantics.

variantsAndExceptions.name: calculationAgent mapping to CalculationAgentIndependent ancillaryParty
variantsAndExceptions.description: Some examples show FPML calculationAgentPartyReference becoming a CDM ancillary party typed 'CalculationAgentIndependent' rather than a straightforward party reference.
variantsAndExceptions.impactOnGeneralization: This appears to be an enrichment/normalization choice; treat as an exception that requires explicit handling or confirmation rather than an automatic party reference mapping.

suspectedEnrichmentOrDefaultBehavior.name: calculationAgentPartyReference -> CalculationAgentIndependent ancillaryParty
suspectedEnrichmentOrDefaultBehavior.description: FPML calculationAgent references are turned into an ancillaryParty entry with role 'CalculationAgentIndependent' in the CDM (appears to be an enrichment or normalization).
caution: Representation changes party reference semantics; require confirmation whether this is always desired or only for specific agent types.

suspectedEnrichmentOrDefaultBehavior.name: payer/receiver role normalization
suspectedEnrichmentOrDefaultBehavior.description: The translation from FPML buyer/seller to CDM payer/receiver may include normalization logic that inverts or reinterprets roles.
caution: Observed inversion or unexpected assignment of payer/receiver; treat as a potential enrichment or domain-specific reinterpretation and validate against business rules.
